title: Timothy Scott (actor, born 1955)
source:
{{Short description|American actor and dancer (1955–1988)}}
'''Timothy Scott Schnell''' (September 15, 1955{{citation needed|date=June 2019|reason=Even if true, a secondary source to confirm the birthdate is needed.}} – February 24, 1988), often credited as '''Timothy Scott''', was an American Broadway actor and dancer. He was born in [[Morton Grove, Illinois]], to parents Richard and Rosemary.<ref name=sun-times/> He died of AIDS-related complications in [[Los Angeles]] at age 32.<ref>{{cite news|work=[[St. Petersburg Times]]|date=March 3, 1988|page=7B|title=Deaths Elsewhere}} Record no. 194.</ref><ref name="LA Times">{{cite news| url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1988-03-01-mn-56-story.html| title=Obituaries: Timothy Scott, 32; Danced in Hit 'Cats'| date=1 March 1988| newspaper=[[Los Angeles Times]]}}</ref>

He portrayed Mr. Mistoffelees in the original 1982 Broadway production of the musical, ''[[Cats (musical)|Cats]]'' "for about 18 months."<ref>{{cite news |title=Other deaths...: Timothy Scott |work=Bluefield Daily Telegraph |agency=Associated Press |page=A-2 |date=March 2, 1988 |via=NewspaperArchive.com }}</ref> He appeared in both [[A Chorus Line|the Broadway stage]] and [[A Chorus Line (film)|the film]] versions of ''A Chorus Line''. He also appeared in other theatre works, including ''[[Dancin']]'' and ''[[King of Hearts (musical)|King of Hearts]]''. Other film and television productions included ''[[Baryshnikov in Hollywood]]'', ''[[Captain EO]]'', the [[52nd Academy Awards|1980 Academy Awards]] and commercials.<ref name=sun-times>{{cite news|date=February 28, 1988|title=Timothy Scott Schnell - originated ''Cats'' role |page=57 |newspaper=[[Chicago Sun-Times]]}} Record no. CHI281629.</ref>

Scott lived with his partner, film editor [[Norman Buckley]].<ref name="LA Times"/><ref>{{cite news |title= Applause 2013: The Texas diva |work=[[Dallas Voice]] |date=August 23, 2013|first=Mark |last=Lowry |url= https://www.dallasvoice.com/applause-2013-texas-diva/ |accessdate=December 19, 2018}}</ref>
